---
title: "Committing"
---

## Making commits

Each time you want Git to take a snapshot of your project, you create a **commit**. A good commit has:

1. A logical, focused set of changes — not everything all at once
2. A short, meaningful message — *what* changed, and *why*?

| ❌ | ✅ |
|---|---|
| *"Fix"* | *"Fix legend label overlap in volcano plot"* |
| *"change colours"* | *"Change bar graph palette to improve contrast"* |
| *"updates"* | *"Add QC filtering step before normalisation"* |

::: {.callout-important}
Commit messages are notes to your future self — who will not remember what *"fixed it"* means!
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
Commit early, commit often. Small, focused commits are far easier to understand — and undo — than one giant commit at the end.
:::

## Bash workflow

```bash
# Navigate to your project and initialise Git
cd my_project
git init

# Check what Git can see
git status

# Stage a specific file and commit
git add filename
git commit -m "Your commit message here"

# View the commit history
git log --oneline
```

::: {.callout-important}
`git add .` stages *everything* in the folder. Use it only after setting up your `.gitignore` — otherwise you may commit files you didn't mean to.
:::

## GUI workflow

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Python (VSCode)

1. Open your project folder in VSCode
2. Click the **Source Control** icon in the left sidebar (`Ctrl+Shift+G`)
3. Click **Initialise Repository**
4. Files appear with **U** (untracked) badges
5. Hover a file and click **+** to stage it — badge changes to **A**
6. Type a commit message in the box at the top
7. Click **Commit** (✓)

### R (RStudio)

1. Go to **File → New Project → Existing Directory**
2. Navigate to your project folder and click **Create Project**
3. Go to **Tools → Project Options → Git/SVN**
4. Change version control system to **Git** and click OK
5. Restart RStudio — the **Git tab** appears top-right
6. Files appear with **?** (untracked) badges
7. Tick the checkbox next to files to stage them — badge changes to **A**
8. Click **Commit**, write a message, click **Commit**

:::

## In practice

::: {.callout-caution}
### Exercises

2.1 Initialise a `git` repository within the `spacewalk_analysis` folder

2.2 Create a `.gitignore` — which files should you exclude?

2.3 Make your first commit with the original folder components

2.4 Write a `README.md` that describes the project, then commit your changes
:::

## Quick reference

| Action | Command |
|---|---|
| Initialise a repo | `git init` |
| Check status | `git status` |
| Stage a file | `git add filename` |
| Stage everything | `git add .` |
| Commit | `git commit -m "your message"` |
| View history | `git log --oneline` |
